title: Use a flat xref table for FTR dependencies
rationale: Flat strings round-trip cleanly through the current JSON and ODS tooling.

title: Keep the project_memory workspace pinned to the current package release
rationale: Document the current repo pin as spreadsheet-handling==0.2.0 for the next release cycle.

title: Visible spreadsheet payload is a string substrate; typing is opt-in metadata
rationale: Closed the 0.2 release-readiness cutline gate by architectural decision rather than code: both backend parsers already stringify cell payload at the table-block boundary, so the string contract is a chosen narrowness, not forced ignorance. Typing stays opt-in via the Cell Codec transformation family. Three non-disruptive migration paths and five revisit criteria are recorded in the ADR. Terminology update (2026-07-20, not a reopening of this decision): the Cell Codec projection-family slice (FTR-META-ONTOLOGY-REMOVAL-WORKBOOK-PROJECTION-EPIC-P4A) retired the _meta.cell_codecs metadata schema surface this rationale originally pointed to; opt-in typing intent is now explicit-only step configuration (codec_intent/mode passed at the call site), with no metadata root or fallback. The decision's substance (string substrate, opt-in typing) is unchanged.

title: Reset domain/meta around a Functional-Model-derived bridge DSL
rationale: After the June-2026 requirement inquiry and Functional Model promotion, the implemented domain/meta surface was judged materially larger and more sedimented than the Functional Model requires. The accepted direction is to tolerate breaking domain/meta changes while external adoption is low, derive a smaller bridge DSL from Functional Model use cases, preserve useful adapter/parser/renderer boundaries, use consumers as coverage checks rather than golden masters, allow targeted deletion of obvious duplicate paths, and avoid recreating the current registry-scale surface under new names.

title: Pause Review 005 domain-contract/meta-reference implementation work after Slice 1d
rationale: The slice sequence proved the intended control-loop mode; further registry expansion should wait for a concrete failing contract or later review, not continue by default.

title: Use validate_references.rules_path as the first consumer-operability slice
rationale: rules_path removes duplicated reference-rule declarations without introducing a broad configuration DSL, a ruleset registry, or a plugin purge.

title: Guard parser canonical writes before adapter/render implementation work
rationale: A parser canonical-write allowlist protects persistent presentation payload and documents the boundary before any adapter/render rewrite or broader meta simplification.

title: Domain boundaries defend proportionately to their contract, not against arbitrary in-process hostile Python
rationale: Accepted repository-wide policy from documentation-only Slice 1 of FTR-DOMAIN-BOUNDARY-ROBUSTNESS-P4A (independent acceptance review 001, 08afe70). A domain boundary must robustly handle malformed and unusual values reasonably implied by its pandas/NumPy/configuration/metadata/artifact contracts, but in-process validation is not a security sandbox: the framework does not promise to contain arbitrary hostile executable Python already admitted into the process. Framework and workflow-builder responsibilities are both load-bearing and neither excuses the other. Cheap local hardening that narrows accepted vocabulary, normalizes at ingress, establishes ownership, or simplifies diagnostics stays in scope; hardening that only defends the excluded hostile-object threat or obscures the domain flow is out of scope. Feature reviews apply this shared boundary and may still report concrete violations of explicit guarantees (immutability, deterministic ordering, exact identity, deliberate diagnostics, failure atomicity, no caller-graph mutation) even when found adversarially, but must not silently expand a feature's threat model. Runtime extraction of a shared helper requires a demonstrated second consumer and its own narrow FTR.

title: Judge Human Readability by bounded reconstruction and contract cost, not mechanical proxies
rationale: Provisional review-method direction from the three-family Human Readability investigation, accepted in Independent Review 001 as provisional and non-normative (0 Blocking, 0 Important, 4 Minor). Macroarchitecture and local Human Readability are independent, complementary quality dimensions: a reader should be able to reconstruct current semantics, lifecycle, ownership, constraints, validation/side-effect order, and non-local reasons within sound architecture, but local simplification cannot override public, persisted, lifecycle, ownership, or architecture contracts. 'Narrow' means the smallest coherent owned domain value (Enrich resolved policy, XRef dense-axis descriptors), not maximal scalar atomization. Vocabulary follows the actual object and boundary: a domain frame should not casually be called a sheet, but a real workbook target or persisted _meta.derived.sheets namespace remains sheet vocabulary. Algorithmic locality and validation order can outweigh file/function length; type stable owned lifecycle states but keep opaque cell/pandas/carrier/persisted-metadata boundaries truthfully heterogeneous. The durable method compares human reconstruction cost against contract/compatibility cost, architecture/ownership cost, maintenance/change cost, and algorithmic locality. It rejects mechanical universal rules: no minimum API or parameter count, no scalar atomization, no maximum file/function length, no global Any or sheet prohibition, no single mandatory import spelling, no mandatory extraction, no mandatory configuration objects/dataclasses, no comments for every empty/no-op path, and no procedural expansion of idiomatic Python. Observations are not findings; findings are not automatic tasks; architecture-gated issues transfer to their owner; implementation requires explicit authorization; independent acceptance stays distinct; accept, defer, coordinate-elsewhere, and stop-here remain semantically distinct. The Human Readability Sentinel is only a provisional future specialized reviewer role (future-human-maintainer perspective; records concrete reconstruction costs and positive patterns; recognizes contract gates; may recommend accept/defer/coordinate/stop-here) — not implemented, not mandatory, not an autonomous refactorer, not a static rule set, and not superior to architecture or public-contract authority. build_v2_target_registry is accepted low-value, load-bearing residue, not active work. This decision is non-normative: it creates no guide, workflow rule, static check, or runtime change.

title: Trusted runtime precondition, independent input authority, and operator-owned security policy
rationale: Independently accepted (Architecture Review 002, 0 Blocking/0 Important/0 Minor, f9ae278) after one narrow enforcement-timing correction (Review 001 finding I-001, resolved in d6be68b). Extends ADR-DOMAIN-BOUNDARY-ROBUSTNESS with five durable constraints extracted narrowly from accepted Technical Concept 001 (Trusted Ingress, Internal Value Model, and Runtime Security Profiles): the trusted runtime/operator precondition (same-process arbitrary Python is not sandboxed against an operator who controls the process, CLI, environment, installation, and import path; this is the framework's threat-model boundary, not a gap); independent payload-trust and pipeline-description-trust dimensions, with all four trust combinations architecturally representable and no public profile name adopted; operator-owned security policy supplied outside untrusted pipeline input, which may only be narrowed, never widened, by that input; per-policy-kind combination semantics (allowlist intersection, numeric minimum/cap, permission conjunction/removal, parameter-schema intersection, reject on widening/unknown/contradictory/incomparable requests) together with a capability-activation timing invariant that permits safe authorization-preparation normalization (parsing, structural validation, policy-owned metadata lookup, resource-identifier canonicalization) before the decision while requiring rejection before any operation that activates, acquires, or exercises the governed capability (module import, executable binding/instantiation, invocation, resource acquisition, sink use); and output-sink capability ownership kept separate from payload normalization, illustrated by (not deciding) the current XLSX leading-`=` formula behavior and the maintained filesystem writers' path containment. Does not decide public profile names, a policy API/class/schema, parser/resource limits, the internal scalar/value type model, missing/unresolved/error representation, the domain.ingress mechanism, the public run_pipeline boundary, the FTR-PIPELINE-DOTTED-EXTENSION-SURFACE-P4A outcome, an untrusted-pipeline allowlist, XLSX formula/literal-text policy, or deployment/process isolation; ADR-VISIBLE-CELL-TYPING-STRING-SUBSTRATE is unchanged and not reopened. No FTR or BUG is authorized by this decision.

title: Classify safely before inspecting a boundary value
rationale: Generalized learning from independently accepted Trusted Ingress E1 (118a164): an as-yet-unclassified boundary value must not participate in proving its own admissibility through candidate-controlled protocol or reachable type/metaclass behavior. Establish bounded carrier-family membership first, then permit only the bounded carrier-specific inspection owned by that accepted family, then admit or reject. This is not a simplistic ban on isinstance and not a generic claim that issubclass is safe. Current E1 anchors on type(value) and uses issubclass(actual_type, accepted_types) only against a closed reviewed set whose production metaclass/subclass semantics are standard; arbitrary future right-hand superclasses, generic reflection/security utilities, and arbitrary hostile in-process Python are outside that proof. Low-level-looking Python primitives require evidence of their actual dispatch semantics at a trust boundary. Safe diagnostics follow the same rule: exact rejected runtime type names are not required, and bounded constant detail is preferable when reflection could execute unsupported behavior.

title: Adopt the Domain Maintainer Contract as the canonical procedure for bounded Domain-family hardening
rationale: Independently promoted after a full design/review/correction/promotion lifecycle (design fefe7f4; independent review 73c990f, verdict MATERIAL REVISION REQUIRED with 1 BLOCKER -- Local Human Readability absent from the completion gate; correction 68c64ea; closure review 8b45d2a, verdict ACCEPT WITH MINOR CORRECTIONS; promotion 7e8c49c; independent promotion verification 3eee351, verdict VERIFIED, no findings). The DMC governs how a bounded Domain area is hardened: no whole-Domain taxonomy or family census is required up front; a family/owner follows semantic and metadata/lifecycle coupling, not module co-location or shared _meta storage; compatibility with existing behavior is evidence-based rather than automatically preserved or discarded; material handoffs between capabilities must be made explicit; Local Human Readability is a first-class, executable completion concern; and independent review is required at each stage. Applied for the first time to the FK/reference-helper family (Cycle 0 plus its first hardening slice, both independently reviewed and closed SLICE COMPLETE); see CONC-DOMAIN-BOUNDARY-ROBUSTNESS for the pilot evidence trail.
